text: Vernon's test, a guideline he credits to Evans, is whose job the consistency is ("Ask Whose Job It Is", Part II of the essay, p. 3): if it is the job of the user issuing the command to make the data consistent, the rule belongs inside; if it is another user's job or the system's, it may be eventually consistent and belongs outside, as a policy (section 8.5).
author: Vaughn Vernon (guideline credited to Eric Evans)
title: Effective Aggregate Design, Part II
locator: Part II, p. 3, "Ask Whose Job It Is"
verification: Re-verified 2026-11-06 against the live source (curl + pdftotext/grep, or browser).
evidence: 'ask whether it's the job of the user executing the use case to make the data consistent. If it is, try to make it transactionally consistent, but only by adhering to the other rules of aggregate. If it is another user's job, or the job of the system, allow it to be eventually consistent.' ('Discussing this with Eric Evans revealed a very simple and sound guideline.')
